a.title: Kentucky Civil Liberties Union plans court action on behalf of Associated Students
a.body: The Herald reported the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union planning court action on behalf of Associated Students, under a headline that also named The Fly, a separate WKU underground newspaper active that year. The archive does not yet hold the article's text, so the underlying dispute is not yet confirmed.

b.title: Associated Students endorses the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union lawsuit
b.body: The Herald reported that Associated Students formally endorsed the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union's lawsuit, a month after the Herald first reported the union planning court action connected to the organization and The Fly.

a.title: Moore questions freshman candidates' campaign spending
a.body: President Bob Moore publicly questioned how freshman class candidates were spending their campaign money. The Herald ran an editorial the same week, 'Bob Moore's Comment Isn't Good Politics,' pushing back on his remark.

b.title: 'A$G?' - Moore questions freshman campaign spending
b.body: President Bob Moore publicly questioned spending by freshman candidates, in a story the Herald headlined 'A$G?'. The paper answered with an editorial arguing that Moore's comment was not good politics, and Moore wrote back disputing it.

a.title: ASG appoints a council to decide disputes
a.body: ASG appointed a council to decide internal disputes. The same issue reported that the regents bill, changing how the student regent was chosen, had passed the state House.

b.title: ASG sets up a council to settle its own disputes
b.body: The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had appointed a council to decide disputes inside the organization. The story ran two weeks after the same reporter, Kevin Francke, covered the resignation of ASG president Marcel Bush.

a.title: Student government conference set for the weekend
a.body: The Herald announced that a student government conference would run from Friday through Sunday. The notice appeared in the 26 March 1987 issue.

b.title: ASG prepares to host the second statewide student government conference
b.body: The Herald reported on 26 March 1987 that ASG would be host, from the following day through Sunday, to the second annual statewide student government conference, at the American Plaza on Scottsville Road. President Tim Todd expected about 50 student leaders, against about 65 at the first conference, which ASG had also hosted, and said hosting would cost between $400 and $500. Registration was $18 and the conference was open to all students. Saturday seminars were to cover leadership, communication and financial aid, with the Council on Higher Education flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington and sending its director, Gary S. Cox.

a.title: ASG bill funds a "President for a Day" fundraiser
a.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-09-F, providing for a "President for a Day" fundraiser.

src.label: SGA Legislation, Bill #91-09-F, "President for a Day"

b.title: ASG bill funds renovation of its own chambers
b.body: The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-03-F, providing for the renovation of the ASG chambers.

a.title: A new store on campus
a.body: SGA proposed a new store on campus, reported by the Herald in early March as the organization kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring.

b.title: A campus store proposal followed
b.body: SGA proposed a new store on campus, the Herald reported, as the association kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring. A week earlier the paper had covered its wish to see the next university president promoted from within.

a.title: Bill proposes an SGA Information Technology Director
a.body: SGA considered Bill 99-10-F, creating a new SGA position of Information Technology Director.

b.title: SGA created an Information Technology Director
b.body: Bill 99-10-F created the SGA position of Information Technology Director, and the same month produced a bill amending the constitution to include website guidelines. The association was formalising its web presence as the decade closed.

a.title: Fall senate election fills 11 seats with 977 votes cast
a.body: SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 new senators elected including Christopher Costa, Corey Johnson and Mallory Treece. Twenty students ran for the seats and 977 students voted. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he got the contested race he wanted.

b.title: Fall senate election draws 977 voters for 11 seats
b.body: Results of the fall senate election were announced just after midnight, with 11 senators elected from a field of 20 candidates. A total of 977 students voted. Those elected were Kelley Boothe, Hannah Garland, Corey Johnson, Elizabeth Wininger, Mallory Chaney, Mallory Treece, Kevin Asbery, Christopher Costa, Jordan Campbell, Nolan Miles and Ross Nowland.

a.title: SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall spending
a.body: The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid and $12,000 for scholarships. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment.

b.title: SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall semester
b.body: SGA approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, of which $43,476.17 remained. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell said the organization had spent roughly $54,000 the previous fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment. The budget was divided into operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $5,500 in stipends already spent.

a.title: SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad application fee
a.body: The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, set to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach; the University Senate passed a similar resolution. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded Study Abroad scholarships failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest.

b.title: SGA opposes the new $150 study abroad application fee
b.body: SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad and Global Learning application fee, which was to begin with summer 2013 programs. Executive Vice President Keyana Boka said SGA took a formal stance because the fee had come up so suddenly. The University Senate had also passed a resolution against the fee, seeking to delay it until fall 2013.

a.title: SGA finalized $125,000 budget
a.body: SGA finalized a $125,000 budget for the 2013-14 year, funded from student tuition at about $6.25 per student, after a planned funding increase did not come through. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each. The executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves.

b.title: SGA finalizes a $125,000 budget with no planned increase
b.body: SGA finalized a 2013-14 budget of $125,000 drawn from student tuition, after not receiving a planned increase. Director of Public Relations Laura Harper said the figure equated to $6.25 per student. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay, who built the budget, said senate discretionary spending required a senate majority and executive discretionary spending required an executive committee majority.

a.title: Mid-year budget report showed $46,883 surplus
a.body: SGA's mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus on its $125,000 budget. The Senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index, and approved Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart as new senators as six senate seats remained open.

b.title: Budget report shows a $46,883.62 surplus
b.body: SGA released its 2013-14 budget showing $125,000 budgeted and a surplus of $46,883.62. Administrative Vice President Nicki Seay said the budget had changed little since December and that she had more funds to allocate back to the student body. SGA allocated $54,000 to the legislative branch for items such as organizational aid and grants, and approved three new senators at the same meeting.

a.title: Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution
a.body: The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, but the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued it was unfair to ban smoking for students required to live on campus for two years. Senators retained the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote.

b.title: Executive Cabinet vetoes the smoke-free campus resolution hours after it passes
b.body: Resolution 11-14-F supporting a smoke-free campus passed the senate 14-10, and the Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Author William Berry said he left the location of any smoking areas to the administration and that the ban infringed no student's rights, while senator Haley Jones countered that smoking is legal and students over 18 can buy tobacco. The policy would not have limited other tobacco products or electronic cigarettes.

a.title: Ransdell formally responded to four SGA resolutions
a.body: President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions on limited smoking, campus alcohol sales, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. He announced a six-person ad hoc committee to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017 and a restaurant in the Garrett Conference Center that could serve beer in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval.

b.title: Ransdell answers four SGA resolutions by email to faculty and staff
b.body: President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff with his official response to four SGA resolutions covering limited smoking, amending the alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct for students over 21, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. On smoking he said he would form a six-person ad hoc committee of students, faculty and staff to recommend how to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017. On alcohol he said a restaurant facility in the Garrett Conference Center would be built where beer and possibly wine could be served.

a.title: Senate opposed state tuition-freeze bill
a.body: The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years. Richey argued such freezes were "dangerous risks" that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. At the same meeting, Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, about $1,301.

b.title: SGA opposes state tuition-freeze bill; Richey says he appointed 42 percent of the senate
b.body: Resolution 2-16-S, opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75's four-year tuition freeze, passed after debate, with Richey arguing such measures "can end up wrecking universities and charging students even more in the long run." Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, a loss of $1,301.27. Richey also told senators appointments should be more democratic, noting he had appointed 42 percent of the sitting senate.

a.title: Senate passed a required sexual assault education resolution, 29-1
a.body: Resolution 1-17-F, co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three senators, supported adding a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to freshman colonnade requirements, arguing existing options like HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. The senate also funded a "No-Shave November" beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws.

b.title: Senate votes 29-1 for a required sexual assault course in the Colonnade
b.body: Resolution 1-17-F, supporting the addition of a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to Colonnade requirements for first-year students, passed 29-1 with two abstentions. Co-author William Hurst said a student could pass four years at WKU without any sexual assault training, calling that "a disgrace, to say the least." Senator Alex Sergent described the resolution as closing holes in an existing net rather than adding a graduation hurdle.

a.title: Budget passes unanimously with spending stipulations
a.body: All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a compromise added stipulations restricting the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributing any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. The budget's passage let Bills 1-19-F (Greeks Go Green) and 2-19-F (funding for Bowling Green Pride) pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates.

b.title: Budget passes with spending stipulations; senate halves campaign spending caps
b.body: All 13 senators approved the budget after a three-part stipulation confined the special projects fund to First Year Village plans and set a March 3 reversion formula. The senate also halved election code campaign maximums, previously $300 for president, $125 for the vice presidencies and $50 for senators, over objections from Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds, who called SGA turnout "awful" and estimated 1,500 students voted the previous year. Senator Symone Whalin said poorer students were less likely to run for executive office.

a.title: Senate approves $5,000 hammocks project
a.body: The senate voted to pass Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was deemed too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris ran so SGA would be known for more than "scantrons and greenbooks". Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek criticized having to vote without seeing budget numbers, and the senate retained power to halt spending during planning.

b.title: Senate approves $5,000 hammock project after volleyball court dropped
b.body: The senate passed Bill 3-20-S allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to plan hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court was judged too expensive earlier in the year. Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek said he had encountered friction getting budget figures from Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds and wanted assurance the money would be spent inclusively. Residence Hall Association President Emily Whitney backed the project and noted RHA's own budget cuts.

a.title: Senate confirmed the year's budget
a.body: At the third meeting of the 21st Senate on Sept. 7, SGA passed Bill 1.21f, confirming its budget for the year. Dean of Students Martha Sales spoke on leadership, and Wininger announced a planned donor drive in partnership with at least four other student organizations. Chief of Staff Parker Raybourne announced a Hilltopper Hangout event for Sept. 24.

b.title: Bill 1.21f confirms the year's budget
b.body: The third meeting of the 21st senate passed Bill 1.21f, confirming the budget for the year. Dean of Students Martha Sales opened the meeting telling senators "we have to learn how to lead" and pressing them on their purpose as a student body. President Matthew Wininger announced a donor drive in partnership with at least four other student organizations.

a.title: Sam Kurtz elected on an unopposed ticket
a.body: With Salvador Leon as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president.

b.title: Kurtz ticket elected unopposed
b.body: Sam Kurtz, the outgoing administrative vice president, was elected student body president on a ticket that ran unopposed, with Salvador León as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president. Fourteen at-large senators and college, class, first-generation and Gatton seats were also filled. Results were read shortly after midnight in the DSU senate chambers by Chief Justice Justin Goins.

a.title: 23rd Senate seats Judicial Council and committee heads
a.body: At its first meeting of the fall semester, SGA approved President Sam Kurtz's nominations of Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the 2023-2024 Judicial Council after what Kurtz called a record number of applicants. Kurtz also announced seven committee heads, including Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. The new appointees took the oath of office at the meeting.

b.title: Kurtz seats five-member Judicial Council and committee heads
b.body: Student Body President Sam Kurtz nominated Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the 2023-24 Judicial Council at the first fall meeting. Kurtz said a record number of students applied and were interviewed over the summer before the field was narrowed to five. Rush Robinson was named head of the Campus Improvements and Sustainability Committee and Karley Solorzano head of the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee.

a.title: Senate voted to rename DEI Committee
a.body: Senators unanimously passed Bill 21-25-S, a constitutional amendment restructuring the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee and renaming it the Action and Opportunity Committee, following President Trump's executive order dismantling DEI mandates. The meeting initially lacked the 21 members needed for a two-thirds vote, so absent members were called onto Zoom to reach quorum. The amendment then went to a student referendum during the April 13-15 election.

b.title: Senate renames DEI committee after scrambling for quorum
b.body: Bill 21-25-S restructured the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee as the Action and Opportunity Committee and retitled Chief Diversity Officers as Chief Engagement and Opportunity Officers, following Trump's executive order dismantling DEI mandates. Rush Robinson moved to table the bill to the fall, but senators chose to vote; with fewer than the 21 members needed present, they phoned absent officers to join by Zoom before passing it unanimously. Co-author Gammons called the change mostly a formality and said a loss of federal funding had been alluded to as a possible issue.
